subject: Accounting
title: Pass-Through Entities
description: A fast breakdown of Pass-Through Entities for builders.

hook.text: Most U.S. businesses don't pay corporate tax. Their profits 'pass through' to personal returns.

buildup.text: Sole proprietorships, partnerships, and S-corporations are pass-through entities.

discovery.text: Business income flows to the owner's personal tax return, taxed at individual rates.

twist.text: This means a small business owner's tax bill depends on their personal bracket, not a corporate rate.

climax.text: Pass-throughs represent over 90% of U.S. businesses and a huge share of total business income.

punchline.text: Most businesses aren't taxed as businesses at all.

quiz.question: What is a pass-through entity?
options: A business whose income is taxed on the owner's personal return
A corporation with special tax breaks

details.summary: Pass-through entities — including sole proprietorships, partnerships, S corporations, and LLCs — don't pay corporate income tax themselves. Instead, their profits 'pass through' to owners' personal tax returns, avoiding double taxation.
details.whyItMatters: Over 90% of U.S. businesses are structured as pass-throughs, and understanding how they're taxed is essential for anyone starting or running a business.
takeaways: Pass-through entities include sole proprietorships, partnerships, S corps, and most LLCs
Business income passes through to owners' personal returns and is taxed at individual rates
This avoids double taxation — corporate tax plus dividend tax — that C corporations face

faq.question: What is a pass-through entity?
faq.answer: A pass-through entity is a business structure where profits and losses flow directly to the owners' personal tax returns rather than being taxed at the business level. Sole proprietorships, partnerships, S corporations, and most LLCs are pass-through entities.

faq.question: Why do most businesses choose pass-through structures?
faq.answer: Pass-throughs avoid double taxation. C corporations pay corporate tax on profits and then shareholders pay tax again on dividends. Pass-throughs skip the corporate tax — profits are taxed only once on the owners' personal returns, often resulting in a lower total tax burden.
